newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-BHW drops plan to buy Postbank stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BHW drops plan to buy Postbank stake.

text.p: German property finance group BHW Holding AG said on Tuesday it had dropped plans to buy a stake in Postbank because of unacceptable demands made by the soon-to-be-privatised bank.
BHW, which has long said it wanted a close co-operation with Postbank, said Postbank had changed the terms of the link-up to such an extent that it no longer made economic sense.
"The matter is over for us," BHW chief executive Reinhard Wagner told a news conference.
BHW, floated in 1996, has been a rising star on the stock market and is set to join the MDAX index of top 100 German shares in the autumn.
The ability to sell BHW products over Postbank's counters in post offices across Germany would have been very important to BHW, Wagner said.
A stake purchase would have been further evidence of the consolidation that has engulfed Europe's financial services industry.

BHW would now concentrate on expanding its own sales force and would keep a lookout for other cooperation deals. BHW also expected "new alliances" in the insurance sector where it wanted to provide services for insurers.
Postbank, Germany's largest savings bank earmarked for sale to the private sector next year, said it regretted BHW's decision.
"A promising partnership with BHW could have developed," a Postbank spokesman said in response to a Reuter enquiry.
The spokesman said Postbank had not yet decided on a partner in the mortgage finance sector and that the Wuestenrot group was the only remaining candidate at present.

BHW's Wagner said Postbank's demands for cooperation were neither acceptable nor promising. Postbank had demanded that BHW drop its independent market presence, a move that would have condemned the BHW brand to a "no name product."

In addition, Postbank had wanted BHW to use its sales teams to win customers for Postbank products but did not want to let BHW serve those customers in BHW's own branches. Postbank had also asked for managerial control over BHW sales teams.
BHW also said it had sold its remaining 10.5 percent stake in DSL Holding AG, a state-controlled bank, as it no longer fufilled any strategic function.

BHW only last week said it had reduced its DSL stake to around 10.5 percent from 20.69 percent. The shares had gone to several German banks, Wagner said, noting that current market conditions made a sale of the shares attractive.
He did not name the banks but said Postbank may be among them. Postbank said it did not have a stake in DSL at present.
